title: Scared Kaomoji (((;ꏿ_ꏿ;))): Copy & Paste Frightened Text Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste scared kaomoji: trembling (((;ꏿ_ꏿ;))), peeking ┬┴┬┴┤(･_├┬┴┬┴, startled Σ(ﾟロﾟ), sweating (・_・;) and fleeing ε=ε=ε=┌(;ﾟДﾟ)┘ text faces.
hero_tagline: Shaking, hiding, screaming and running away, all drawn in text. Tap a frightened face and it lands on your clipboard.
intro: A scared kaomoji shows fear through three tricks. Stacked brackets like ((( ))) are motion lines, so the whole face reads as shaking. A wide-open mouth such as Д or ロ is a gasp or a scream. A semicolon beside the face is a bead of cold sweat. Faces peeking around ┬┴┬┴┤ are looking out from behind a wall, and ε=ε=ε= is a dust trail left by someone running off. People use these for horror films, jump scares, exam results and any message they are nervous to open. For the 😨 😱 picture versions, see the scared emoji page linked below. A few faces use Yi or Lao letters for the eyes, and an older device may draw those as boxes.

sections.label: Trembling
sections.intro: The extra brackets on each side are the shake. More brackets means a harder tremble.

sections.label: Hiding
sections.intro: Half a face behind a wall or a door: the reader is too frightened to come out fully.

sections.label: Startled
sections.intro: Σ in front of a face is a jolt line from manga, the mark drawn when a character jumps.

sections.label: Nervous
sections.intro: Quieter fear: dread, unease and the cold sweat before bad news.

sections.label: Running Away
sections.intro: The ε= marks are the dust cloud behind a fleeing figure, so these read as moving left to right.

faq.q: What do the brackets around (((;ꏿ_ꏿ;))) mean?
faq.a: Each extra bracket is a motion line, the way a comic artist draws vibration around a shaking character. The semicolons are sweat drops and ꏿ, a letter from the Yi script, gives the big round eyes.

faq.q: What does ガクガク mean next to a kaomoji?
faq.a: ガクガク (gakugaku) is Japanese onomatopoeia for trembling or knees knocking together. Put in front of a shaking face, it spells out the fear in sound as well as in shape.

faq.q: What is the difference between a scared and a shocked kaomoji?
faq.a: A shocked face like Σ(ﾟロﾟ) is a single moment of surprise and can be good news. A scared face adds signs of fear that last: shaking brackets, sweat, hiding behind a wall or running away.
